name: 寿司・しゃぶしゃぶ ゆず庵 新宿西口大ガード店 (Sushi & Shabu-shabu Yuzuan Shinjuku Nishiguc)

claims.text: The Monogatari Corporation allergy information page for the Yuzuan brand lists the seven mandatory allergens (wheat, buckwheat, egg, dairy, peanut, shrimp, crab) per menu item and says items not yet listed can be investigated on request, typically within about two weeks.
Publishes a chainwide, regularly updated allergen chart covering the seven major allergens for its menu items, which diners can consult before ordering.

name: 丹想庵 健次郎 (Tansouan Kenjiro)

claims.text: Two soba noodle types are hand-cut fresh each day — a nihachi (80% buckwheat/20% wheat) and an inaka (country-style) noodle — both containing wheat by recipe; no gluten-free or 100%-buckwheat noodle was found offered.
The English-speaking owner and his wife ran a Japanese restaurant in New York for 33 years and are experienced at hosting international guests, including visitors from Zambia, Germany, and Australia.
A vegan banana cake is listed as a standing menu item alongside items like pandan latte, indicating at least some intentional plant-based options are offered rather than being incidental.

name: 十和田 メトロ通り店（手打ちそば十和田） (Teuchi Soba Towada (Metro-dori Branch))

claims.text: The tsuyu (dipping sauce) is made fresh in-house daily using only real bonito flakes, with no chemical seasonings or additives — a point of pride for flavor quality, though it is fish-based, not vegan.

name: This is Crêpe（ディスイズクレープ） (This is Crepe)

claims.text: Not applicable as a cross-contact question in the usual sense — the standard crêpe batter is itself made with French wheat flour, so gluten is a base ingredient rather than an incidental contaminant, and no gluten-free batter option was found.

Tofu and yuba are made fresh in house daily from soybeans and Chichibu spring water rather than bought pre-made, which at least limits hidden mass-produced additives in the tofu itself (sauces and broths are a separate, unconfirmed question).

Multiple independent write-ups describe the kintsuba filling as made from just Tokachi (Hokkaido) azuki beans, sugar, and water — cooked down and carefully skimmed of impurities — suggesting a short, visible ingredient list for the signature item.
